about: The release and change conventions register of The UOR Foundation, projected by conventions/project.mjs from conventions/scan.json and the pinned specifications and Foundation norms. Every repository has one outcome per convention; every mandatory or conditional convention that is unmet or unobserved is an open claim.

norms.statement: This document summarizes the naming, versioning, and tagging conventions enforced across all UOR Foundation repositories. Commit messages: [Conventional Commits v1.0.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/).
All Tier 1 and 2 repositories follow [Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/):
Publish release notes for every tagged release.

clauses.statement: Software using Semantic Versioning MUST declare a public API. This API could be declared in the code itself or exist strictly in documentation. However it is done, it SHOULD be precise and comprehensive.
clauses.how: states what a release means or contains; not decidable from a tag or a manifest

clauses.statement: A normal version number MUST take the form X.Y.Z where X, Y, and Z are non-negative integers, and MUST NOT contain leading zeroes. X is the major version, Y is the minor version, and Z is the patch version. Each element MUST increase num...
clauses.how: the FAQ regular expression on every candidate version

clauses.statement: Once a versioned package has been released, the contents of that version MUST NOT be modified. Any modifications MUST be released as a new version.
clauses.how: states what a release means or contains; not decidable from a tag or a manifest

clauses.statement: Major version zero (0.y.z) is for initial development. Anything MAY change at any time. The public API SHOULD NOT be considered stable.
clauses.how: any 0.y.z is allowed; nothing a version string says can break it

clauses.statement: Version 1.0.0 defines the public API. The way in which the version number is incremented after this release is dependent on this public API and how it changes.
clauses.how: states what a release means or contains; not decidable from a tag or a manifest

clauses.statement: Patch version Z (x.y.Z | x > 0) MUST be incremented if only backward compatible bug fixes are introduced. A bug fix is defined as an internal change that fixes incorrect behavior.
clauses.how: states what a release means or contains; not decidable from a tag or a manifest

clauses.statement: Minor version Y (x.Y.z | x > 0) MUST be incremented if new, backward compatible functionality is introduced to the public API. It MUST be incremented if any public API functionality is marked as deprecated. It MAY be incremented if subst...
clauses.how: states what a release means or contains; not decidable from a tag or a manifest

clauses.statement: Major version X (X.y.z | X > 0) MUST be incremented if any backward incompatible changes are introduced to the public API. It MAY also include minor and patch level changes. Patch and minor versions MUST be reset to 0 when major version ...

clauses.statement: Precedence refers to how versions are compared to each other when ordered.
clauses.how: the item 11 comparator on every tag series and changelog, against semver.compare

clauses.statement: Commits MUST be prefixed with a type, which consists of a noun, `feat`, `fix`, etc., followed by the OPTIONAL scope, OPTIONAL `!`, and REQUIRED terminal colon and space.
clauses.how: the header grammar

clauses.statement: The type `feat` MUST be used when a commit adds a new feature to your application or library.
clauses.how: states what a commit means or how an implementor reads it

clauses.statement: The type `fix` MUST be used when a commit represents a bug fix for your application.
clauses.how: states what a commit means or how an implementor reads it

clauses.statement: A scope MAY be provided after a type. A scope MUST consist of a noun describing a section of the codebase surrounded by parenthesis, e.g., `fix(parser):`
clauses.how: the header grammar

clauses.statement: A description MUST immediately follow the colon and space after the type/scope prefix. The description is a short summary of the code changes, e.g., _fix: array parsing issue when multiple spaces were contained in string_.
clauses.how: the header grammar

clauses.statement: A longer commit body MAY be provided after the short description, providing additional contextual information about the code changes. The body MUST begin one blank line after the description.
clauses.how: the second line of a message with a body is blank

clauses.statement: A commit body is free-form and MAY consist of any number of newline separated paragraphs.
clauses.how: the body is free-form

clauses.statement: One or more footers MAY be provided one blank line after the body. Each footer MUST consist of a word token, followed by either a `:<space>` or `<space>#` separator, followed by a string value (this is inspired by the [git trailer conven...
clauses.how: footers are optional and a trailing paragraph is body when it is not footers

clauses.statement: A footer's token MUST use `-` in place of whitespace characters, e.g., `Acked-by` (this helps differentiate the footer section from a multi-paragraph body). An exception is made for `BREAKING CHANGE`, which MAY also be used as a token.
clauses.how: a line that is not token-and-separator is body, so the footer grammar cannot be broken

clauses.statement: A footer's value MAY contain spaces and newlines, and parsing MUST terminate when the next valid footer token/separator pair is observed.
clauses.how: as item 9

clauses.statement: Breaking changes MUST be indicated in the type/scope prefix of a commit, or as an entry in the footer.
clauses.how: a breaking change may be in either place; the footer form is checked by item 12

clauses.statement: If included as a footer, a breaking change MUST consist of the uppercase text BREAKING CHANGE, followed by a colon, space, and description, e.g., _BREAKING CHANGE: environment variables now take precedence over config files_.
clauses.how: a BREAKING CHANGE footer is uppercase and followed by a colon, a space and a description

clauses.statement: If included in the type/scope prefix, breaking changes MUST be indicated by a `!` immediately before the `:`. If `!` is used, `BREAKING CHANGE:` MAY be omitted from the footer section, and the commit description SHALL be used to describe...
clauses.how: the header grammar

clauses.statement: Types other than `feat` and `fix` MAY be used in your commit messages, e.g., _docs: update ref docs._
clauses.how: states what a commit means or how an implementor reads it

clauses.statement: The units of information that make up Conventional Commits MUST NOT be treated as case-sensitive by implementors, with the exception of BREAKING CHANGE which MUST be uppercase.
clauses.how: the BREAKING CHANGE footer check, which reads the token case-insensitively and requires it uppercase

clauses.statement: BREAKING-CHANGE MUST be synonymous with BREAKING CHANGE, when used as a token in a footer.
clauses.how: BREAKING-CHANGE is read as BREAKING CHANGE by the footer check

clauses.statement: Changelogs are for humans, not machines.
clauses.how: a judgement on the prose

clauses.statement: There should be an entry for every single version.
clauses.how: every-version: each SemVer tag of the main series has a version heading

clauses.statement: The same types of changes should be grouped.
clauses.how: change-types: every ### heading is one of the six types

clauses.statement: Versions and sections should be linkable.
clauses.how: linkable: every bracketed heading has a link reference definition

clauses.statement: The latest version comes first.
clauses.how: latest-first: dates do not increase and SemVer precedence decreases down the file

clauses.statement: The release date of each version is displayed.
clauses.how: version-headings and iso-8601-dates

clauses.statement: Mention whether you follow Semantic Versioning.
clauses.how: semver-mentioned

clauses.statement: Types of changes: Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security.
clauses.how: change-types

clauses.statement: Keep an Unreleased section at the top to track upcoming changes.
clauses.how: unreleased-first

clauses.statement: Call it CHANGELOG.md.
clauses.how: the file at the repository root, case-sensitive
version-headings accepts the [YANKED] suffix and no other

clauses.statement: Dates formatted like 2017-07-17 (ISO 8601) are the recommended format.
clauses.how: iso-8601-dates: YYYY-MM-DD and a calendar date
